name: isocitrate dehydrogenase (NADP(+)) 1

function.text: IDH1 encodes a cytosolic and peroxisomal NADP-dependent enzyme that converts isocitrate to alpha-ketoglutarate and generates NADPH.

germline.text: The sources reviewed for this pilot do not establish an inherited IDH1 cancer-predisposition syndrome. Ollier disease and Maffucci syndrome are associated with postzygotic somatic mosaic IDH1 variants and should not be described as germline disorders.

somatic.text: Somatic IDH1 mutations occur in diffuse gliomas, acute myeloid leukemia, and cholangiocarcinoma. Cancer-associated R132 variants can acquire a neomorphic activity that produces D-2-hydroxyglutarate; their significance must be interpreted within the specific disease context.

somatic_associations.mechanism: Somatic IDH1 mutations; R132 variants may have neomorphic activity.

function.text: IDH1 encodes an NADP-dependent isocitrate dehydrogenase located mainly in the cytoplasm and peroxisomes. The enzyme converts isocitrate to alpha-ketoglutarate, also called 2-oxoglutarate, while generating NADPH. Cytoplasmic NADPH production and regeneration of NADPH within peroxisomes are important aspects of its normal function. Its subcellular location distinguishes IDH1 from the related mitochondrial NADP-dependent enzyme encoded by IDH2.

mosaic.text: Postzygotic mosaic variants are associated with Ollier disease and Maffucci syndrome.

somatic.text: Somatic IDH1 mutations occur in diffuse gliomas, acute myeloid leukemia, and cholangiocarcinoma. Cancer-associated R132 variants can acquire a neomorphic activity that produces D-2-hydroxyglutarate.
